P1 Only current keys go in the patatt keyring; retired keys drop out at the next export (patatt has no validity window). Revoked keys always out.
P2 Eligibility: any registered human with at least one endorsed email (D2), regardless of tier. Only endorsed emails become identities. No endorsed email = absent (patatt shows no key).
P3 Automation (bot) keys ARE allowed in the patatt keyring (this widens automation from 'files only' to files + patches; git tags/commits still excluded). Follow-on (Claude, for review): a bot qualifies when it holds the automation tier and its email is endorsed, normally by its accountable maintainer; no new mechanism."}

{"notes":"DECIDED (Mark, 2026-10-22):
P1 Only current keys go in the patatt keyring; retired keys drop out at the next export. Revoked keys always out.
P2 Eligibility: any registered person with at least one endorsed email, regardless of tier. Only endorsed emails become identities.
P3 Automation keys allowed (automation now signs files + patches, never git tags/commits); a bot qualifies when its email is endorsed, normally by its accountable maintainer.
P4 Selector derived from the key ('k-' + short fingerprint) for every key; exact derivation fixed after the spike; git vouch status prints it.
P5 Published as a branch in the registry repo, regenerated after each merge, fetched by git vouch sync, read via patatt.keyringsrc=ref:...; follow-on (Claude): git-vouch-patatt --check regenerates locally and reports differences so the regenerator is auditable.
Recorded in DESIGN.md 'Patch signing' section and Tools table."}
